title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Issuing the Several Opinions on Implementing Legal Supervision over Civil Trial Activities and Administrative Litigation (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Circular on Issuing the "Several Opinions on the Implementation of Legal Supervision over Civil Adjudication Activities and Administrative Litigation (for Trial Implementation)"

Gao Jian Hui [2011] No. 1

To: The Higher People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In order to implement the central government's reform task of "improving the scope and procedures for procuratorial organs to exercise legal supervision over civil and administrative litigation," the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate have formulated the "Several Opinions on the Implementation of Legal Supervision over Civil Adjudication Activities and Administrative Litigation (for Trial Implementation)." This document is hereby issued to you, and you are requested to strictly comply with it. If any issues arise during implementation, please promptly report them to the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

March 10, 2011

Several Opinions on the Implementation of Legal Supervision over Civil Adjudication Activities and Administrative Litigation (for Trial Implementation)

Article 1. These Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Constitution and laws, and in light of judicial practice, for the purpose of improving the scope and procedures for procuratorial organs to exercise legal supervision over civil adjudication activities and administrative litigation, and to safeguard judicial fairness.

Article 2. In accordance with Article 14 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 10 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Procuratorates shall exercise legal supervision over civil adjudication activities and administrative litigation.

Article 3. If a People's Procuratorate finds that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement falls under any of the following circumstances, it may investigate and verify the matter with the parties or persons not involved in the case:

(1) It may harm the national interest or the public interest;
(2) A party in civil litigation, or the plaintiff or a third party in administrative litigation, was unable to collect evidence on their own due to objective reasons during the original trial, and the People's Court, upon their written application for investigation and collection of evidence, should have investigated and collected such evidence but failed to do so;
(3) Civil adjudication activities or administrative litigation proceedings violated statutory procedures, potentially affecting the correctness of the judgment or ruling.

Article 4. If a party applies to the People's Procuratorate for a protest before the judgment or ruling of first instance becomes legally effective, the People's Procuratorate shall inform the party to file an appeal in accordance with legal provisions. If a party, after a first-instance judgment or ruling that is appealable becomes legally effective, files a petition, it shall explain the reasons for not having appealed; if there is no正当 justification, the petition shall not be accepted.

Article 5. If the Supreme People's Procuratorate, upon case-filing review, finds that a civil judgment or ruling of a People's Court at any level that has become legally effective, or if a higher People's Procuratorate, upon case-filing review, finds that a civil judgment or ruling of a lower People's Court that has become legally effective, falls under one of the circumstances provided in Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and meets the conditions for a protest, it shall file a protest with the corresponding People's Court in accordance with the provisions of Article 187 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

If a People's Procuratorate finds that a legally effective administrative judgment, or an administrative ruling such as a ruling of non-acceptance, dismissal of an action, or objection to jurisdiction, of a People's Court, falls under the circumstances provided in Article 64 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it shall file a protest.

Article 6. If a People's Procuratorate finds that a legally effective civil mediation agreement or administrative compensation mediation agreement of a People's Court harms the national interest or the public interest, it shall file a protest.

Article 7. If a local People's Procuratorate at any level, with respect to a judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement that meets the circumstances provided in Articles 5 and 6 of these Opinions, after a decision by the Procuratorial Committee, may issue a procuratorial recommendation for retrial to the People's Court at the same level.

After receiving a procuratorial recommendation for retrial, the People's Court shall conduct a review within three months and provide a written reply to the People's Procuratorate regarding the review results. If the People's Court considers a retrial necessary, it shall notify the parties. If the People's Procuratorate considers the People's Court's decision not to retry improper, it shall refer the matter to a higher People's Procuratorate to file a protest.

Article 8. After the People's Court has rendered a ruling rejecting an application for retrial, if the party again petitions to the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall not file a protest against the ruling rejecting the retrial application. If, upon review, the People's Procuratorate finds that the original legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement meets the conditions for a protest, it shall file a protest. If, after trial, the People's Court ascertains that the grounds for the protest are substantially the same as the grounds for the party's rejected retrial application, it may render a judgment upholding the original judgment.

Article 9. If the adjudicative activities of the People's Court violate legal provisions in circumstances other than those provided in Articles 5 and 6 of these Opinions and do not warrant retrial proceedings, the People's Procuratorate shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the People's Court.

If a party considers that the adjudicative activities of the People's Court fall under the circumstances provided in the preceding paragraph and, after raising an objection, the People's Court has not corrected the matter, and the party petitions to the People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall accept the case.

Article 10. If a People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation, the People's Court shall make a disposition within one month and provide a written reply to the People's Procuratorate regarding the status of the disposition.

If the People's Procuratorate disagrees with the reply of the People's Court, it may, through a higher People's Procuratorate, submit the matter to the corresponding higher People's Court. If the higher People's Court considers the opinion of the People's Procuratorate correct, it shall supervise the lower People's Court to make timely corrections.

Article 11. When handling administrative petition cases, if a People's Procuratorate discovers that an administrative agency has acted in violation of legal provisions, which may affect the fair trial by the People's Court, it shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the administrative agency and inform the People's Court of the relevant circumstances.

Article 12. When handling civil or administrative petition cases, if a People's Procuratorate, upon review, finds that the adjudicative activities of the People's Court were lawful and the judgment or ruling was correct, it shall promptly inform the relevant parties of the review results and explain the reasons, and shall perform work to persuade the parties to accept the judgment and desist from further petitions.

When handling civil petition cases or administrative compensation petition cases, if both parties are willing to settle and the conditions for settlement are met, the People's Procuratorate may suggest that the parties settle on their own.

Article 13. When a People's Court hears a protested case, it shall notify the People's Procuratorate to send personnel to appear in court.

The tasks of the procuratorial personnel attending the retrial court are:

(1) To read the protest letter;
(2) To present evidence collected by the People's Procuratorate ex officio, including evidence favorable and unfavorable to the petitioner, and to explain matters raised by the parties.

If the procuratorial personnel discover that the court proceedings are unlawful, they shall, after the conclusion of the court session or an adjournment, report to the Chief Procurator and issue a procuratorial recommendation in the name of the People's Procuratorate.

Article 14. When handling civil or administrative supervision cases, the People's Procuratorate shall perform its duties of legal supervision in accordance with the law, strictly comply with case-handling rules and relevant procuratorial disciplinary norms, shall not seek any private gain, and shall not abuse its supervisory power.

Article 15. If a People's Court discovers that a procuratorial supervision act violates the law or procuratorial discipline, it may submit a written recommendation to the People's Procuratorate. The People's Procuratorate shall, within one month, provide a written reply to the People's Court regarding the results of its handling. If the People's Court disagrees with the reply of the People's Procuratorate, it may, through a higher People's Court, submit the matter to the corresponding higher People's Procuratorate. If the higher People's Procuratorate considers the recommendation of the People's Court correct, it shall require the lower People's Procuratorate to make timely corrections.

Article 16. The People's Procuratorate and the People's Court shall establish corresponding communication and coordination mechanisms to promptly resolve relevant issues arising in practice.
